label: Ubiquiti UniFi Dream Router 5G Max (UDR-5G-Max)
description: UniFi Dream Router 5G Max (UDR-5G-Max) - 5G NR Sub-6 modem (2x nano-SIM + eSIM), 4x 2.5G RJ45 (1 PoE, 15.4 W budget) + 1x 10G SFP+ (10G/1G). WiFi 7; 34.5 W max excluding PoE output.
notes:
Vendor figures from the tech specs page, read 2026-11-19 (structured spec table, not the rendered images): **2.5 GbE RJ45 = 4 (1 PoE) (2.5G/1G/100M)**, **10G SFP+ = 1 (10G/1G)**, **Max. WAN port count 4**, default WAN ports **(1) 10G SFP+ / (1) 2.5 GbE RJ45**, **PoE Budget 15.4 W** with the single PoE port rated 15.4 W (802.3af, 44-57 V), **Max. Power Consumption 34.5 W (excluding PoE output)**, **Cellular: 5G NR Sub-6** - 5G NSA 3.4 Gbps down / 560 Mbps up, 5G SA 1.8 Gbps / 650 Mbps, 4G LTE 1.6 Gbps / 210 Mbps, **(2) Nano SIM + (1) Nano-SIM or eSIM**.

The modem is modelled as `wwan0` at the vendor's 3.4 Gbps 5G NSA downlink, the convention `u5g-max`, `u5g`, `u5g-max-outdoor`, `u-lte-backup-pro` and `umr` already use; the engine resolves the name to a cellular cage and offers LTE / LTE-A / 5G sub-6 media from that rate. Without it the row was a router with four RJ45s and no WAN of the kind the request asks for.

The WiFi 7 radios (2.4 GHz 688 Mbps / 5 GHz 4.3 Gbps / 6 GHz 5.7 Gbps, 2x2) are NOT modelled: no UniFi console row in this catalogue carries radios, and adding them to this one row alone would make the console family read as if only this model had WiFi. The PoE budget and the single port's 802.3af ceiling are the same 15.4 W figure on the vendor page - that is one PoE port, not a budget that happens to match.
